events.title: 2026 IEEE CIS London Symposium on Foundation Models & Evolutionary Intelligence
events.location: Imperial College London, South Kensington Campus (Huxley Building, Room 311)
events.speaker: Prof. Yaochu Jin (IEEE Fellow) & Dr. Marta Garnelo (DeepMind London)
events.summary: Our flagship annual symposium bringing together leading AI scientists across London to explore the synergy between Large Language Models, Evolutionary Optimization, and Multi-Agent Systems.
events.content:
The 2026 IEEE CIS London Autumn Symposium is our premier annual gathering for academics, PhD researchers, and industry practitioners across Greater London.

Key Highlights:
• Morning Keynote: Evolutionary Optimization in the Era of Large Foundation Models
• Afternoon Panel: Safe, Interpretable, and Energy-Efficient Computational Intelligence
• Early-Career & PhD Poster Spotlight Session (Best Poster Award sponsored by IEEE CIS)
• Evening Networking Reception with IEEE UK & Ireland Section leaders.

events.title: Distinguished Lecture & Workshop: Explainable AI (XAI) and Type-2 Fuzzy Logic in Healthcare
events.location: University College London (UCL), Roberts Building G06 & Hybrid via Zoom
events.speaker: Prof. Christian Wagner & UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence
events.summary: An interactive technical workshop examining how interpretable fuzzy inference systems and neuro-fuzzy architectures enable trustworthy clinical decision support in NHS trials.
events.content:
Trustworthiness and interpretability remain critical barriers to deploying black-box deep learning models in high-stakes healthcare environments.

In this IEEE CIS Distinguished Lecture hosted at UCL, we explore how modern Type-2 Fuzzy Systems combined with deep representation learning provide transparent, uncertainty-aware clinical predictions. Hands-on Python notebooks and benchmark datasets will be shared with all attendees.

events.title: London Student & Young Professionals (YP) Summer Colloquium on Bio-Inspired Computing
events.location: King's College London, Strand Campus (Bush House Auditorium)
events.speaker: IEEE CIS London Chapter Executive Committee & Industry Mentors
events.summary: Over 120 PhD candidates and early-career researchers gathered at King's College London for lightning talks, career mentoring, and collaborative hackathons.
events.content:
The Summer Colloquium showcased groundbreaking student research from KCL, Imperial, UCL, Queen Mary, Brunel, and City University of London.

Topics spanned spiking neural networks for neuromorphic hardware, swarm intelligence for autonomous urban drones, and multi-objective evolutionary design. Three Outstanding Student Paper Awards were presented during the closing ceremony.

events.title: Spring Technical Seminar: Graph Neural Networks & Complex Dynamical Systems
events.location: The Alan Turing Institute, British Library, London NW1 2DB
events.speaker: Dr. Pietro Liò & London Graph Learning Research Group
events.summary: Deep-dive seminar on geometric deep learning, spatio-temporal graph neural networks, and applications to London transport and smart grid optimization.
events.content: Hosted in collaboration with peers at The Alan Turing Institute, this seminar explored theoretical advances in message-passing neural networks, topological deep learning, and scalable graph transformers applied to real-world urban infrastructure.

topics.title: Deep Learning, Neural Architectures & Neuromorphic Computing
topics.lead: Neural Networks Technical Committee (London Working Group)
topics.summary: Investigating next-generation neural architectures, continual learning, neuromorphic spiking systems, and theoretical foundations of deep representation learning.
topics.content:
As one of the three foundational pillars of the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society, our London Neural Networks working group focuses on bridging theoretical neuroscience, mathematical foundations of deep learning, and energy-efficient hardware deployment.

### Current Research Priorities
1. **Continual & Lifelong Learning**: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in non-stationary environments.
2. **Neuromorphic & Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs)**: Event-driven computation for ultra-low-power edge intelligence.
3. **Physics-Informed & Geometric Neural Networks**: Embedding domain symmetries and physical conservation laws into neural architectures.

### How to Get Involved
We organize bi-monthly reading groups and joint special sessions for IJCNN and IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (TNNLS). Contact the working group chair to propose a seminar topic.

topics.title: Evolutionary Computation, Swarm Intelligence & Automated ML
topics.summary: Harnessing Darwinian evolution and collective swarm behavior for black-box optimization, Neural Architecture Search (NAS), and evolutionary prompt engineering.
topics.content:
London and the broader UK have a rich heritage in Evolutionary Computation. Our chapter actively advances population-based metaheuristics, genetic programming, and multi-objective optimization.

### Key Focus Areas
1. **Evolutionary Neural Architecture Search (ENAS) & AutoML**: Automatically discovering compact, high-performing deep architectures.
2. **Many-Objective & Dynamic Optimization**: Solving complex real-world engineering, logistics, and sustainable energy scheduling problems.
3. **Synergy of LLMs and Evolutionary Search**: Using evolutionary algorithms to guide code synthesis, heuristic discovery, and agentic reasoning.

Members regularly contribute to the IEEE Congress on Evolutionary Computation (CEC) and IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation (TEVC).

topics.title: Fuzzy Systems, Uncertainty Quantification & Trustworthy AI
topics.summary: Computing with words, human-centric interpretable rule bases, Type-2 fuzzy logic, and hybrid neuro-fuzzy reasoning for safety-critical systems.
topics.content:
As AI regulations in the UK and Europe increasingly demand transparency and accountability, Fuzzy Systems play a vital role in translating complex numerical data into human-understandable linguistic rules.

### Core Themes
1. **Neuro-Fuzzy Hybrid Systems**: Combining the learning power of deep neural networks with the transparent reasoning of fuzzy rule bases.
2. **Interval & General Type-2 Fuzzy Logic**: Modeling higher-order epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty in noisy sensor environments.
3. **Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support**: Applications in finance, autonomous driving safety validation, and medical diagnostics.

topics.title: Emerging Topic: Cognitive & Agentic Systems in Financial and Urban Ecosystems
topics.lead: Industry & FinTech Liaison Group (City of London)
topics.summary: Bridging academic computational intelligence with London's world-leading financial district and smart infrastructure initiatives.
topics.content:
Uniquely positioned in London, our chapter fosters close collaboration between university laboratories and R&D teams in the City of London, Canary Wharf, and Knowledge Quarter (King's Cross).

### Active Initiatives
• **Computational Intelligence for Quantitative Finance**: Evolutionary portfolio optimization, market microstructure simulation, and anomaly detection.
• **Resilient Urban Systems**: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for traffic flow, electric vehicle grid balancing, and climate resilience.
• **Algorithmic Fairness & Governance**: Ensuring computational intelligence aligns with IEEE Ethically Aligned Design standards.
